findings.title: Negative upgrade check points at the marketplace instead of the plugin
findings.trigger: Follow the documented negative check after a Claude Code update from a throwaway directory.
findings.execution_path: The command passes .claude/plugins to --plugin-dir, but that directory contains the marketplace manifest. The plugin manifest and hooks are under .claude/plugins/planchk-router.
findings.consequence: The check can fail to load the guard being tested, producing a misleading upgrade failure and preventing the documented procedure from validating fail-closed behavior.
findings.evidence: The changed tree places plugin.json and hooks below planchk-router; the repository's research example also specifies --plugin-dir pointed directly at that plugin directory. Existing tests load hook files directly and cannot catch this README error.
findings.suggested_fix: Use --plugin-dir /path/to/triggarr/.claude/plugins/planchk-router and verify the disposable session actually exposes the intended BM checker before testing refusal.
findings.hypothesis: Claude's direct plugin loader will not load the nested router when given only its marketplace parent. Live CLI execution was not performed.

limitations: Did not rerun pytest in the read-only sandbox; relied on the supplied exact-head harness evidence.
Did not execute Claude Code or model-gateway integration; actual module loading, model availability, and fallback behavior remain unverified.
The guard proves only the environment flag value, not successful module registration. The README acknowledges residual routing verification.
Plugin tests are not invoked by the inspected CI commands.
Command entries containing multiple shell commands report the overall shell exit code.
